🧱 Frequently asked questions

How many models and categories does the LEGO WeDo 2.0 catalog contain?

The catalog covers 597 models for the LEGO Education WeDo 2.0 core set (45300), grouped into 26 categories: official LEGO instructions, animals, dinosaurs, robots, mechanisms, space, transport, walking machines and models without a smart hub.

How do I search and filter models by theme or keyword?

Use the instant search box in the header or the category sidebar of the interactive catalog. Model names and the interface are available in four languages (Ukrainian, English, Polish and Russian) and switch instantly without reloading the page.

What are the Instruction Roulette and the “I built it!” tracker for?

The roulette picks a random robot to build when kids cannot decide. The “I built it!” mark, star ratings and favourites are stored locally in your browser and unlock playful achievements.

Does the catalog work for free on tablets, smart boards and offline?

Yes. The web app has no external dependencies, is designed for touch screens and works as a PWA with a cached app shell, so it stays reliable during lessons. External PDF instructions open separately in Google Drive or your browser.

Who made the catalog and who owns the rights to the instructions?

All LEGO® and WeDo® trademarks belong to the LEGO Group. The guides are collected for non-commercial educational use only, with no sales or monetization.

What should a child learn after LEGO® Education WeDo 2.0 at ages 8–14?

After visual building and basic sensors, kids usually move on to making games in Scratch (ages 8–10), Python programming in Minecraft (ages 9–13) or 2D/3D game development with Unity and C# (ages 11–17).
